carries: A2 Imagery Rescripting (somatic) and IC1 (inner child)
after: But high-risk trauma work needs a bigger container than that.
text: One such container is a clinical therapy called [Imagery Rescripting](https://ibogaqueen.substack.com/i/201523223/imagery-rescripting), which I go into in my somatic guide. It works a lot like the way I [re-do trauma memories](https://ibogaqueen.substack.com/i/189761959/re-do-trauma-memories) in my inner child reparenting guide, where you imagine a painful memory going differently. Here, though, the therapist is in the scene with you, stepping in as the ideal adult who protects and nurtures your inner child. Over the sessions, you learn to be that adult yourself, so it's what I'd go to for a memory that feels too big to re-do on your own.
after_block: The main clinical practice guidelines for the treatment of major trauma recommend one or more of the trauma-specific variants of cognitive behavioral therapy (often referred to by specific names, such as cognitive processing therapy, prolonged exposure, etc.) or eye movement desensitization and reprocessing, depending on the person and the guideline. These approaches in turn can be further supported by techniques such as self-hypnosis and inner child work. But high-risk trauma work needs a bigger container than that.

carries: A3 Pain That Won't Quit? (somatic) and IC2 (inner child)
section: What It's For, and Not For
text: Pain is one of those symptoms. If yours has lasted months and doctors have found no injury or disease to explain it, I'd look for a therapist trained in Pain Reprocessing Therapy or Emotional Awareness and Expression Therapy, the two talk therapies I go into in [my somatic guide](https://ibogaqueen.substack.com/i/201523223/pain-that-wont-quit), alongside the self-hypnosis. They've helped people with long-lasting back, muscle and joint pain, by changing their relationship to the pain without pretending it's not there.
after_block: Don’t use self-hypnosis to: force yourself to remember trauma, force yourself to prove trauma through memories, push symptoms down instead of getting medical attention, destabilize yourself, or replace appropriate clinical care.

carries: A1 Can't Stay With a Feeling? (somatic)
after: Whatever it is, just do it.
text: In therapy sessions, being too analytical can be a way of getting away from a feeling: you start explaining it as soon as it comes up, or you agree with the therapist just to get past it. If that keeps happening, look for someone trained in Intensive Short-Term Dynamic Psychotherapy, which I go into in my somatic guide's section [Can't Stay With a Feeling?](https://ibogaqueen.substack.com/i/201523223/cant-stay-with-a-feeling). If instead you start to feel unreal, stop for the day, as [Dissociating or Unreal?](#§dissociating-or-unreal) says.
after_block: “What if you didn’t try to improve the practice?” Put one hand on your heart and the other on your solar plexus, as in [the two-hand practice](#§the-two-hand-practice), and say, “I don’t have to do this perfectly. I’m here for a relationship with something deeper than my surface mind.” “What can you do to make this a communion, not a performance?” Maybe it’s silence, resting, or doing something. Whatever it is, just do it.
